paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: nobody gets saved by adding something to Jesus. Those men from Judea said you cannot be saved unless you are circumcised (Acts 15:1). Peter shut that down with one sentence: "we believe it is through the grace of the Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are" (Acts 15:11). Grace is the whole recipe, and nobody gets to sneak extra ingredients in.

Notice how God settled it. He gave the Gentiles the Holy Spirit, and Peter says He "cleansed their hearts by faith" (Acts 15:8-9). God knows the heart, so He doesn't need our extra paperwork. And when the church wrote its letter, they said it "seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us" (Acts 15:28). They listened to what God was already doing, and then they lined up with it.

So what do you do with this, baker? Don't stack rules on top of somebody's faith and call it the gospel, and don't let anyone stack them on yours. Hold grace tight, and then handle the hard stuff like this church did: talk it through, listen to each other, and send encouragement. The people in Antioch read that letter and rejoiced (Acts 15:31). I just told you grace is enough, and I'd bet you're rejoicing a little too.
